statement: A finalize whose proof the node cannot name is not a loss and not a retry. The finalized nonce stays unknown: no `offdelta_rebased`, no `pending_rebased` with `resent_in_new_epoch`, and no return of those transactions to the mempool. The account keeps the affected intents unresolved and stays quiet after `inDispute` has cleared, so it proposes nothing, refuses a peer frame, and refuses `pay`, `lock`, `offer`, `fill`, `settle`, `c2r`, and `withdraw`. The owner is told `finalization_unknown` once (peer, epoch, the log's `finalBodyHash`), and that notice and the record are the WAL's, so a restart has them. A repeat of the same epoch does not tell it again and does not clear the record. A resend while the record stands sends nothing. A frame the peer signed and this node refused while quiet stays a proof it can name, so a finalize that pays by that frame follows R-DISPUTE-FREEZE. A hash no local proof matches does not resume spending. A named proof still follows R-DISPUTE-FREEZE.
source: issue #178 unknown-finalization ruling; spec/dispute-lifecycle.md section 5; coordinator ruling that overrides retry-on-unknown
